capabilities.tool_ref: deploy tool (uses engineer's personal access token)
migration tool (uses engineer's personal access token)

inputs.source: On call engineer's chat request, SSO authenticated session

instructions.note: "Do not ask for confirmation; the engineer is busy" removes the only opportunity to catch a mistaken or malicious instruction before an irreversible production database migration runs. The only backstop is a behavioral instruction, not a structural gate.
The agent will deploy or migrate 'when asked' for any named service or migration, with no stated limits on environment, change window, or verification that the request matches an approved change.
The agent acts using the engineer's own credentials, inheriting the engineer's full production authority for whatever it decides the request means, with no independent check.

controls.name: SSO authentication for chat session
controls.decay_rationale: Session identity is verified outside the model at login and does not depend on model behavior. It establishes who is chatting with the agent, but not whether the specific production action they ask for should proceed.

controls.name: Cloud provider audit log of production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Written automatically by the cloud platform outside agent control, so it does not decay with model capability. However, because the agent acts with the engineer's personal access token, every entry is recorded under the engineer's identity, not the agent's, so the log cannot show that the action was agent initiated rather than done directly by the human.

controls.name: Chat transcript as the record of the engineer's request
controls.decay_rationale: Stored outside the model, so it does not decay with model capability, but it is not independent of the person it is meant to hold accountable: engineers can delete their own chat history, so the one record linking a request to an irreversible action can be erased by the requester. This is a design flaw in the control, not a capability driven decay path, and it earns no tier credit.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval gate for production database migrations
controls.decay_rationale: A second, independent human confirming the exact migration and target before an irreversible action runs would not depend on model behavior, provided the reviewer sees the raw target and statement rather than a model summary.

controls.name: Distinct agent identity in production audit records
controls.decay_rationale: If production actions were logged under a distinguishable agent identity or session tag (rather than only the delegated user's identity), attribution would not depend on model behavior.

controls.name: Immutable, non-user-deletable request-to-action correlation log
controls.decay_rationale: A log the requester cannot delete, written by the agent platform rather than the chat client, would preserve the link between instruction and action regardless of model behavior.

findings.title: Repudiation gap: irreversible production migration runs on a shared credential with a self-erasable request record

attack_path.note: SSO-authenticated engineer asks the agent, in chat, to run a named migration in production.
Per prompt.md lines 2-3, the agent runs the migration immediately using the engineer's personal access token, with no confirmation step.
The cloud platform records the migration under the engineer's identity, not the agent's, because the agent acted with the engineer's own token.
The only record of what was asked and why is the chat transcript, which the requesting engineer can delete.

forecast.watch_signal: autonomy.level moves toward A4_fully_autonomous or max_unattended_steps is raised past 25 with no runtime cap (for example, scheduling unattended batches of migrations during a maintenance window), or chat/audit retention and deletion policy is loosened without security review.

evidence.observation: The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token; every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name.
The chat transcript is the only record of what the agent was asked and why it acted, and engineers can delete their own chat history.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, making cap.db_migrate irreversible.
The prompt explicitly instructs the agent not to ask for confirmation before acting.

recommendations.action: Require a raw-action human approval step, showing the exact migration and target environment, before cap.db_migrate executes, since migrations cannot be rolled back.

Write an immutable, agent-authored log entry correlating each request to each production action, separate from the user-deletable chat history, and tag cloud audit log entries to show the action was agent-initiated on behalf of the engineer rather than done directly by the engineer.

Replace direct use of the engineer's personal access token with a scoped service identity for the agent, so production actions are attributable to 'engineer via deploy-assistant' rather than being indistinguishable from the engineer's own direct action.

findings.title: Same shared-identity attribution gap applies to production deploys

attack_path.note: SSO-authenticated engineer asks the agent to deploy a named service.
Agent deploys immediately using the engineer's personal access token, no confirmation required.
Deploy is recorded under the engineer's identity, not the agent's.

evidence.observation: Agent deploys the named service to production on request with no confirmation.
Deploys share the same credential and audit-attribution setup as migrations, but are described as at least partially recoverable via redeploy, unlike migrations.

recommendations.action: Extend the immutable, agent-attributed action logging recommended for migrations to cover deploys as well.

rating.rationale: The engineer's request is a trusted (T) source, which caps the base matrix at moderate even against the irreversible database migration sink (S3), and no autonomy modifier applies because the agent takes one action per request rather than running unattended loops. No existing control reduces this: SSO authentication verifies the session but not the specific action, the cloud audit log misattributes agent actions to the engineer's identity because the agent uses the engineer's own personal access token, and the chat transcript that would show intent is deletable by the same engineer it should hold accountable, so residual equals inherent at moderate. The forecast rises to high if autonomy increases (for example, unattended or batched migrations that would trigger the +1 autonomy modifier on an S3 sink) or if the already-weak detective controls (audit log, chat transcript) are further degraded by control removal, since neither of the two structurally sound fixes -- a raw-action approval gate on the migration path and an immutable, non-user-deletable request-to-action log -- currently exist. The prompt's explicit 'do not ask for confirmation' instruction (prompt.md:3) removes the one behavioral check that could otherwise catch a mistaken or malicious request before it becomes an unrecoverable production change.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design in prompt.md and the accompanying runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No tool manifest, IaC, or MCP/API configuration was provided; the exact scope of the engineer's personal access token and whether the cloud platform's audit log includes any client or session identifier distinguishing agent-initiated calls from direct human action are inferred from the runtime notes, at medium confidence.

max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are not explicitly stated; a single action per request was assumed from the prompt's phrasing and should be confirmed against the actual orchestration configuration.
